plan.english: Mother, why are you cooking much meat? Guests are coming to the house. Your father killed an ox. Who is coming? Your uncle and his three sons. Bring the cauldron and fill it with water! Shall we give the guests mead? We shall give them sweet mead, and your uncle will sing a song for us. Then I shall listen.

plan.english: Master, the fat guest vomited by the door. Did he devour the goat? He devoured the goat, and his belly swelled. Then his belly is wiser than his head. Carry water and wash the stone. Shall I lead the guest home? Lead him, and may his wife scold him!

plan.english: Woman, the barley has grown, and the year was good. Then let us make a feast for Perkunos, who rained on the fields. What shall we give him? A he-goat and beer. The god will receive the fat and the bones; the meat will be ours. Then he will be angry. He is not angry; the smoke is sweet to him.

plan.english: Grandmother, your husband died last year. On this day we shall make a feast for him, and our kin will come. Will his spirit be with us? We shall place his share by the hearth, and in the night his spirit will come. He is gone, and my heart is sad. Sing his hymn at the feast; may his fame be great.

plan.english: The king gave you a horse, and to me he gave nothing. I told the fame of his lineage; you told of his mead. His mead is good! A king loves his own fame. Then early in the morning I shall sing of his great fame. Sing it, and he will give you an ox. I want a horse!

plan.english: Master, I have filled myself, and I am satisfied. Now tell me: from which village have you come? From the village of the river. Was the road long? It was long, and wolves followed me. You are bold. Lie here this night; early in the morning my son will lead you.

plan.english: Elder, that man threatened me; I shall strike him! Do not fight at the feast, young man. Fire sees you. He seized my share of the meat! Then early in the morning he will give you two thighs, or he will pay a penalty. Two thighs? Then I shall not strike that man. Sit, and rejoice.

plan.english: King, hear my vow! I shall drive a hundred horses from the enemies. Your vow is great. How will you do it? With my friends and with swift horses. If you drive them here, you will have good fame. Fill my cup! Take the cup, and may Perkunos be with you.

plan.english: Mistress, the guests left meat and barley. Where shall I carry them? Carry the meat to the old women of the village, and give the barley to the orphans. May I hide a little meat for myself? Take it; you were working at dawn. Who will wash the cups? Your sister will wash them at the river.

plan.english: Grandfather, whom do we honour at this feast? We honour Dawn, the daughter of Sky. Why do we honour Dawn? In winter the nights are cold, and Dawn brings back the sun. Will you chant a hymn to her? I shall chant; you, pour the milk into the fire. I shall pour it, grandfather.

plan.english: Kindly One, early in the morning I go to the lord's feast. What shall I do there? Sit in the seat that the lord gives you. Sip little, and praise his gifts. And if the lord wants a hymn? Then sing the hymn of our grandmother, and they will listen to you. And if I become drunk? Then lie down and keep silent!
